bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly to Annual Conversion

When planning your finances, knowing how your hourly rate translates to an annual salary is essential. The basic formula is straightforward: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and superannuation.

### The Basic Formula

For a standard full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the calculation is:

Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52

For example, if you earn $30 per hour:

$30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year

Your weekly pay would be $30 × 38 = $1,140, and your fortnightly pay (weekly × 2) would be $2,280. This is a useful figure for budgeting and comparing salary offers.

### Why 38 Hours?

The Fair Work Act defines a standard full-time week as 38 hours. However, many awards and agreements set different ordinary hours. Always check your specific award or contract. Our [the timesheet](/) calculator lets you adjust hours to match your situation.

## Average Salary Australia by Age: Benchmarking Your Earnings

Understanding the **average salary Australia by age** helps you see where your pay sits relative to others in your age group. The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) releases average weekly earnings data by age bracket, but these figures are national averages and may not reflect your specific job or location.

### State Differences in Ordinary-Time Earnings

ABS data shows that full-time adult ordinary-time earnings vary across states and territories. For example, the national average weekly ordinary-time earnings for full-time adults was $2,083.70 in May 2026, but state averages can be higher or lower due to industry mix and cost of living. While we don't publish state-specific figures here, our [reference tables](/data) include state-level averages from the ABS to help you compare.

Remember: these are averages, not medians for your job. Your actual pay depends on your industry, experience, and employer. The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour (or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). Many employees are covered by award rates that are higher than the minimum.

## Tax and Superannuation Considerations

Your gross annual salary is not what you take home. Tax and the Medicare levy are deducted, and superannuation is paid on top by your employer.

### Tax Brackets for 2026–27

The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) sets the following resident tax rates for 2026–27:

- Nil on income up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a 2% Medicare levy (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds, as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page for an estimate after tax and Medicare.

### Super Guarantee

Your employer must pay superannuation at 12% of your ordinary earnings (from 1 July 2026) on top of your salary. This is not deducted from your pay. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, and stops once your earnings exceed that cap.

## Distinguishing Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

It's important to know the difference between the National Minimum Wage, award rates, and casual loading:

- **National Minimum Wage**: $26.44 per hour (38-hour week). This is the legal floor for employees not covered by an award.
- **Award rates**: Many industries have specific minimum pay rates set by the Fair Work Commission. These are often higher than the national minimum. Check your award via our [pay guides](/blog) or the Fair Work Ombudsman.
- **Casual loading**: Casual employees receive an extra 25% on top of the base rate (or award rate). For the national minimum, that's $33.05 per hour. Our [the timesheet](/) calculator has a checkbox to add casual loading. **Do not** type a rate that already includes loading; use the base rate and tick the box.

Super is paid on top of ordinary earnings, including the casual loading amount.

## Using Our Tools

### The Timesheet Calculator

Our [the timesheet](/) home page lets you enter your base hourly rate and choose whether to add 25% casual loading. It then calculates your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay, plus estimated tax and super. It assumes 38 hours per week unless you change it.

### Pay Guides and Reference Tables

For award-specific rates, visit our [pay guides](/blog). For state and national average earnings, see our [reference tables](/data). These resources help you benchmark your pay against industry and location averages.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

By understanding the **average salary Australia by age** and how your hourly rate converts, you can make informed career and financial decisions. Use our tools to see where you stand.
